free_tier.stated: No free tier. The site offers a 7-day risk-free period that it describes as a refund, not a trial: 'you can try it risk-free for 7 days, without limitations. Not happy? We'll refund your payment'.

per_object_cap.notes: an article size is a protocol convention, not a vendor number

retention.stated: Retention is not stated on the home page read. The r/usenet map records a 3,000-day retention with 1,500-day primary and 1,500-day secondary backfill.

egress.terms: Unlimited volume on the unlimited plans; account sharing permitted; posting enabled by default

interface_detail: NNTP over TLS on port 563; no HTTP or object API exists for the download path, so a user drives it through SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav
tooling: SABnzbd, NZBGet or nzbdav over NNTP/TLS; any newsreader works because the protocol is the same everywhere, and no provider SDK is needed
chaining: Stacks as a cheap fill or as a low-cost primary for recent content; the ASN it shares with UsenetExpress makes it a weaker second feed than its independence suggests.

limits.value: soft 5 TB/month on unlimited plans, reset on request via support - reported, not on the vendor page
3,000 days, reported; not stated on the vendor page

limits_note: Packages start at $1.79/mo with no coupon required, per the vendor. Blocks are sold separately; the r/usenet deals wiki records a 500 GB block at EUR 13.99 and a 2,000 GB block at EUR 18 in a Black Friday listing, neither of which was on the page read.
binding_note: The vendor publishes no volume cap; the reported soft ceiling is 5 TB/month, which 1 TiB/month does not reach.

identity_cost.detail: Email plus a paid plan; the 7-day window refunds a payment rather than avoiding one.

reliability_note: Independent Dutch platform (ViperNews B.V., formerly mapped as Uzo Reto) that has shared an ASN with UsenetExpress since 2023, which makes it a less independent second feed than it looks.
confidence_note: The price floor and the 7-day refund are vendor-stated and read. Retention and the soft cap are third-party only, and retention decides the retrieval verdict, so the record sits at the reported rung.

evidence.proved: 'starting at $1.79/mo'; 'try it risk-free for 7 days'; '7-day money-back guarantee'; account sharing allowed; posting enabled by default
ViperNews backbone: full, cached, primary backfill 1,500 days, secondary backfill 1,500 days; 'soft limits (5tb per month) on their unlimited plans'

notes: A 3,000-day spool is roughly half of Omicron's. For anything older than eight years this provider is the wrong primary.

extras.backbone: ViperNews / Uzo Reto, AS62296 shared with UsenetExpress
